newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share trading quiet as holiday looms.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share trading quiet as holiday looms.

text.p: Trading was slow on the Nigerian stock market on Wednesday as dealers prepared for a long weekend of public holidays to celebrate a Moslem festival.
The all-share index closed at 8789.89 from 8778.39 on Tuesday.
Traders said turnover was slowly improving following the introduction of an automated clearing system on Monday which scared away many brokerages.
"More stockbroking houses traded today than did on the two previous days," said one broker. "Turnover would have been much higher but for the coming holidays."
The market closes Thursday and Friday to mark Eid-El-Fitr.
Blue chips ended stronger in a relentless scramble for leading stocks.
But there was a lull in food and beverages shares, which have been among market leaders recently.
Both Nigerian Bottling Company and Nestle were unchanged at 56.00 naira and 70.15 naira, respectively.
Flour Mills, however, rose five kobo to 14.30 naira while P.S. Mandrides went three kobo up to 5.23 naira.

Conglomerates were in a strong position on favourable investors' perception. PZ Industries added 25 kobo to 29.75 naira, Lever Brothers was 20 kobo higher at 29.80 naira and UAC went 10 kobo up at 19.90 naira.
NAL Merchant Bank was 35 kobo better at 8.25 naira while Industrial Gases shot up 30 kobo to 11.10 naira.
